chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma’il, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from the one he heard from (and he named him), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the alms-tax: What does a man take from it? And I said to him: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'Any man who leaves two dinars, they are to burn between his eyes.' He said: Then he said: Those are a people who were guests to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family), and when evening approached, he would say: 'O so-and-so, go and provide this (person) with evening supper.' When morning approached, he would say: 'O so-and-so, go and provide this (person) with morning breakfast.' They did not fear to wake up without morning food nor without evening food, so one man of them saved two dinars. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said this statement about him: 'Indeed, the people only give from one year to another year, hence, a man may take what suffices for him and suffices for his family from one year to another year.'

key_terms.السَّنَةِ إِلَى السَّنَةِ: From one year to another year (annual basis)
key_terms.دِينَارَانِ: Two dinars (a specific amount of gold currency)
key_terms.كَيُّ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ: Burning between the eyes (a metaphor for severe punishment or stinginess)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on how much zakat a person can take from the public treasury?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes the prohibition of hoarding two dinars as specific to the 'Ibn al-Sabil' (travelers/guests) who received daily sustenance and thus had no need to save, distinguishing them from the general populace. This hadith establishes the jurisprudential principle that ordinary recipients are entitled to take sufficient funds for themselves and their dependents for a full year, rather than being limited to a single day's provision.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al- ‘Attar, from Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ali bin Isma’il, from Safwan, from Abdul-Rahman bin Hajjaj, from the one he heard from, and he named him, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

I asked him about the alms tax: What does a man take from it? And I said to him: It has, indeed, reached us that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Any man who leaves two dinars, they are to burn between his eyes. He said: Then he said: Those are a people who were guests to the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and when the evening approached, he said: O such-a-person, go and feed this (person) the evening supper. When the morning approached, he said: O such-a-person, go and feed this (person). They did not fear to wake up at the morning without food nor without evening supper, and so one man of them saved two dinars. Then the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said this statement about him: Indeed, the people only give from one year to another year, hence, a man may take what suffices for him and suffices for his family from one year to another year.
